children: Chile's central bank trimmed on Wednesday its gross domestic product expectations, with growth now seen between 0.25% and 0.75% for this year, down from its previous range of 1% to 1.75%.
In its prior June report, the bank had already reduced its GDP forecast from a previous range of 1.5% to 2.5%.
• "By 2026, we will see a combination of weaker domestic spending, the negative effects of the weather on various sectors during the third quarter, and lower mining output," the bank said.
• Looking ahead, the bank kept its estimate for economic growth next year between 2% and 3%.

• In its September Monetary Policy Report, the institution also maintained its 2026 average inflation forecast at 3.7%, indicating that weak domestic demand will help mitigate cost pressures caused by rising fuel prices.
• Year-end inflation is seen at 4.3% by December 2026, slightly up from a prior 4.2% estimate, but falling to 2.8% by end-2027.
• Inflation is expected to converge to the 3% target in next year's second quarter, according to the report.
• The bank raised its copper price forecast for 2026, projecting prices of $6.1 per pound, up from a prior $5.8 estimate.
• For 2027, it estimates copper prices at $5.4 per pound, 20 cents higher than its June projection.

title: Chile central bank trims GDP growth estimate again
